hotspots.name: Senate Gallery
hotspots.text: The ʻEwa cone, below this door: Hawaiʻi's 25 senators under the Moon — a chandelier of 620 chambered nautilus shells. The public watches from up here, at the rail.

hotspots.name: House Gallery
hotspots.text: The Diamond Head cone: the 51 representatives under the Sun, a chandelier of gold-plated globes. Every state law begins as a bill read in one of the two cones below.

hotspots.name: Ways & Means
hotspots.text: The Senate's money committee. A revenue bill that cannot clear Ways & Means goes no further.

hotspots.name: House Finance
hotspots.text: The House's money committee — every appropriation in the state budget passes across these tables.

hotspots.name: Governor · Level 5
hotspots.text: The elevator to Level 5, where the Governor and Lieutenant Governor look down into the rotunda. The veto pen lives up there.

hotspots.name: Aquarius
hotspots.text: The floor medallion below marks where Tadashi Sato's sea-stone mosaic lies. Look up instead: no dome — the rotunda opens to the sky. The sky is Hawaiʻi's capitol dome, and rain and rainbows come inside.
